what: The score combines exact insertion distance with depot-radial urgency, Clarke-Wright geometric affinity to the current route, affinity to another customer that can still fit, protection of strong pairs that would be split by capacity, and a one-step residual-capacity packing penalty. It runs in O(len(route) + len(unassigned)) time per evaluated insertion and uses O(1) extra space.
why: The representative layouts contain radial clusters and, in the smaller-capacity cases, substantial demand pressure. The radial and savings terms favor adding distant customers to routes serving the same sector rather than leaving expensive isolated trips for later. The packing term discourages unusable residual capacity, while the blocked-partner term avoids greedily separating a candidate from a stronger future companion. Route affinity is ordering-independent, making it relevant after intra-route 2-opt, while insertion delta still selects a sensible slot. The coefficients are scale-invariant with respect to distance but are heuristic constants; the one-customer packing lookahead cannot detect multi-customer demand combinations, and strong nonradial or highly irregular instances may require different weighting.
